questions.q: Recite «يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالًۭا» (90:6) with each natural madd held for 2 counts.
questions.a: Two natural madds: يَقُولُ (و) and مَالًا (ا), each 2 counts.

questions.q: Which letter is a madd letter in «يَقُولُ»?
Madd hunt (pupil PDF): circle every natural madd in Al-Balad 90:1 to 7. Today's rota group recites 90:1 to 7 to the teacher.
questions.a: For example: بِهَٰذَا (ا), وَمَا (ا), فِى (ي), يَقُولُ (و), مَالًا (ا).

questions.q: Extend: write the three madd letters with the vowel before each.
questions.a: ا after fathah, و after dammah, ي after kasrah.

questions.q: Stretch: why is «لَآ» in 90:1 longer than 2 counts?
questions.a: A hamza starts the next word, so it is madd munfasil (4 or 5 counts), not natural.

questions.q: How many counts is the natural madd?
questions.a: A) 2. Madd tabi'i is always 2 counts: it is the length of the vowel itself.

questions.q: The madd letter ي needs which vowel before it?
Think again: Say 'qala' and then 'qaaala'. Which one changes the meaning, and why does length matter in Arabic?
questions.a: Length matters: a short or over-long vowel can change a word, so each madd has a set count.
